answer: Each identity registers a tide gauge post fitted with a prism and locks an 85-credit bond. Each epoch it submits the prism angle, tide reading, and gale wind speed. An auditor recomputes tide height from a prism table with gale correction, burning the bond over 2 percent error, reused readings, or one prism for two identities. First filing costs 34; kth costs 34+6(k-1), so the 1000th costs 6028 and 1000 fakes cost 3,031,000 plus 85,000 locked. A rented-prism ring fails because prism serial and angle signature bind to one key. Honest identities pay 34 once and recover the bond after audit.
